manifest.configuration_1: Point the app at a Kiro Crew checkout; PR actions need authenticated gh, while pods need systemd --user on Linux, launchd on macOS or Task Scheduler on Windows and must be provisioned first.
manifest.description: A control panel for working on Kiro Crew itself. Lists every feature worktree alongside its pull request state, commit count, and disk usage, and can bring any of them up as a pod: a complete preview instance on its own port with its own data directory, so you can click through an unfinished change without disturbing your live gateway. It also handles the chores around that — pulling main and rebuilding, rebasing a branch, streaming pod logs, and pruning worktrees whose work has already merged. Enabling it also lets AGENT sessions start and stop pods through the pod tools, which means code from a worktree an agent can write runs outside the agent's sandbox, as you.
manifest.highlight_1: Bring up any worktree as an isolated pod on its own port and data directory, leaving your live gateway untouched
manifest.highlight_2: Fleet view with per-branch PR status, commit counts, and disk usage
manifest.highlight_3: Sync (pull main and rebuild) or rebase a branch without leaving the dashboard
manifest.highlight_4: 'Prune merged' refuses to delete a worktree with uncommitted or untracked work rather than discarding it
manifest.highlight_5: Stream pod logs and mint pod access tokens from the UI
manifest.highlight_6: Built for people developing Kiro Crew itself — not needed for everyday use
manifest.highlight_7: Pods run on Linux (systemd --user), macOS (launchd) and Windows (Task Scheduler) — but the macOS pod has no enforced memory/CPU ceiling; Make Live stages its pointer on every platform, and automatic restart needs a systemd --user unit or a macOS LaunchAgent; the fleet view, PR status, sync, rebase and prune work on any platform
manifest.use_case_1: Operate Kiro Crew feature worktrees and isolated preview pods while keeping the live gateway untouched.
